data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"On verifiable tasks, the panel-plus-checklist will reliably outperform the single expert only when the expert's intuition is subject to known biases the checklist explicitly counters; otherwise, the expert's tacit configural knowledge dominates and the panel's additive cue model underperforms.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the expert is unbiased and the task is genuinely configural, the additive panel model fails to capture interactions and underperforms.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the checklist includes interaction terms, it approximates a configural model and the additive/configural distinction collapses.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's bias is unknown, the bias-correction mechanism cannot be verified within a single evaluation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition is a single integrated readout of a configural model learned via extensive exposure; the checklist forces an additive (cue-by-cue) model. Additive models outperform configural models only when the configural model is distorted by bias (e.g. base-rate neglect). The causal mechanism is bias-correction, not aggregation per se. The distinguishing evidence within one evaluation is whether panel advantage concentrates on items where the expert's known bias applies.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
